title: Week of October 12th, 2026. $DELL $XMTR $MPC $TSLA $CON

market_pulse.headline: Indexes shrugged off an AI scare to post a positive week, then started earnings week flat to lower. In the week to Fri Oct 9 the S&P 500 rose about 1.2% after hitting a record 7,844.52 intraday, even though Thursday's report that OpenAI's revenue was lower than earlier figures hit chip and AI stocks. Treasury yields were near 24-year highs and Brent crude stayed above $100. On Columbus Day Monday (Oct 12) the Dow rose 0.38%, the S&P 500 slipped 0.06% and the Nasdaq fell 0.44%, with energy leading. Next up: Q3 bank earnings (Tue/Wed), September CPI (Wed Oct 14), PPI and retail sales (Thu Oct 15), TSMC (Thu) and a speech by Fed Chair Warsh.

- S&P 500: 7,811.54, up 0.59% on the day. Weekly change was +1.15% per Investrade and +1.21% per LPL. It set a record intraday high of 7,844.52 during the week, then eased as yields rose.

Stocks rebounded on Friday.

MONDAY OCT 12, Columbus Day (equities open, bond market closed; light volume) (Investrade 'Market Review: October 12, 2026'; Yahoo Finance live blog Oct 12; TheStreet Oct 12):
- Dow: 51,850.55, +195.60 (+0.38%)
- S&P 500: 7,807.24 (-0.06%)
- Nasdaq Composite: 27,245.90 (-0.44%)
- Russell 2000: 2,794.48 (-0.45%)
- Trading stayed in a tight range all day. Nine of 11 S&P sectors rose, led by Energy. Micron fell 3.9% on rising competition from China's CXMT.
drivers: OPENAI REVENUE SHOCK / AI SELLOFF (Thu Oct 8): The FT reported that OpenAI's annualized revenue was about $50B at the end of September. Earlier reports had put it at about $68-70B; a person familiar told CNBC the higher figure included gross revenue from partners. Chip stocks fell about 3.4%: Intel -5%+, Broadcom -4%+, Oracle -5%+, Nvidia about -3%, CoreWeave -7.8%, AAOI -13.6%. The Nasdaq fell 1.25%. Futures recovered Friday after reports that OpenAI expects to reach or exceed a $70B run-rate by year-end on enterprise growth. (political.org Oct 8; Mitrade/TradingKey Oct 9; TMGM Oct 9; Wealth Professional)

YIELDS AT 24-YEAR HIGHS: The 10-year Treasury yield hit about 5.35-5.36% on Oct 7, a 24-year high, then eased after a solid auction. Closes were 5.22% on Oct 8 (Fed H.15) and about 5.24% on Oct 9 (Streetstats/Investing.com). The 10-year is up about 60bp since end-July. Higher yields capped the S&P's run to a record. Bond markets were closed Monday Oct 12. (CNBC Oct 7; Fed H.15 Oct 9)

FOMC MINUTES (released Wed Oct 7): Officials expect to raise rates further but gave no timing, citing inflation and energy prices. The next FOMC meeting is Oct 27-28; markets put the odds of an October hike below 20% as of Oct 9. (CNBC Oct 7; Nasdaq Chartstopper Oct 9)

JOBS DATA AFTERMATH: The September payrolls report (released Fri Oct 2) was weak: +29K vs about 88K expected, with unemployment up to 4.2% (Yahoo Finance Oct 2). Odds of an October hike fell from about 64% to about 17% (CME FedWatch) and about 18% (Kalshi), but traders still price a hike by December (CNBC Oct 2).

OIL / MIDDLE EAST: Brent settled about $104.72 on Oct 9 (+0.42%, Yahoo Finance BZ=F; Forbes showed $102.78). Brent jumped about 4% on Oct 8 (Mitrade). US crude held just above $90 for the week, and a hurricane threatened US supply. Trump ruled out a strike on Iran before the midterms (Nasdaq Chartstopper Oct 9). US crude has risen about 20% since end-July (CNBC Oct 7). Energy led again Monday Oct 12; a pre-close snapshot showed crude futures up about 2% (Yahoo, unconfirmed settle).

NEW MONDAY OCT 12: Thin holiday session as investors positioned for bank earnings and Wednesday's CPI. The Dow and value/energy names held up while tech and small caps slipped; Micron fell 3.9% on concern about competition from China's CXMT. Early Tuesday (Oct 13): EUR/USD hit a 17-month low as a hawkish Fed and oil lifted the dollar (Vantage Markets Oct 13). JPMorgan reported Q3 EPS of $5.57 vs $5.90 expected, a rare miss; Wells Fargo reported $1.87 vs $1.85 (CNBC live blog Oct 13).
market_pulse.sectors: Leading: Energy, which led Monday Oct 12 on Brent above $100 and Middle East and hurricane risk (Investrade Oct 12). The Dow and other defensive and value groups were also leading: the Dow had its best week since early August and was the only gainer on both Thursday Oct 8 and Monday Oct 12. Lagging: semiconductors, AI infrastructure and AI cloud (Intel, Broadcom, Nvidia, Oracle, CoreWeave, AAOI, and Micron -3.9% Monday), plus small caps (Russell 2000 -0.76% on the week per LPL and -0.45% Monday). Rate-sensitive groups face pressure from a 10-year yield above 5.2%. No source with a full weekly sector ranking for Oct 5-9 was found (null).
market_pulse.breadth_sentiment: The mix is a cautious record-high market, not euphoria. The S&P 500 is within about 0.5% of its 7,844.52 record, but the Nasdaq-100 and the 10-year yield were roughly flat for Oct 5-9 (Nasdaq Chartstopper Oct 9), and the Russell 2000 lagged (-0.76% on the week, LPL). That points to narrow, megacap- and Dow-led gains. Monday's breadth was positive by sector (9 of 11 S&P sectors up) even though the Nasdaq and Russell fell. Main sentiment risks are doubts about AI monetization after the OpenAI report, yields at 24-year highs, and the Fed's hiking bias. VIX, AAII and put/call readings were not found in dated sources (null).

week_ahead: Tue Oct 13: Q3 bank earnings kick off before the open with JPMorgan (EPS $5.57 vs $5.90 est., a rare miss, per CNBC live blog Oct 13), Wells Fargo ($1.87 vs $1.85 est.), Goldman Sachs (est. about $13.04) and Citigroup (est. about $2.65 EPS on about $23.7B revenue). Fed Gov. Waller is on a Bloomberg New Economy Forum AI panel (3:45am ET). Boston Fed's Collins spoke Monday night (8pm ET).

Wed Oct 14: September CPI at 8:30am ET, the week's key print. Headline is expected at about 3.6% y/y vs 3.4% prior, about 0.6% m/m vs 0.4% (TradingView/Stocktwits and FXEmpire previews; consensus varies by source). Bank of America and Morgan Stanley report. ASML reports, a read on AI capex. Fed Gov. Bowman speaks at the IMF meetings in Bangkok.

Thu Oct 15: PPI and retail sales at 8:30am ET (one calendar has core retail sales at +0.5% m/m vs +1.4% prior). TSMC Q3 earnings are a key AI and semiconductor test after the OpenAI scare. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh holds a fireside chat with IMF MD Kristalina Georgieva at the IMF Annual Meetings in Bangkok; Investing.com and ZeroHedge date it Thu Oct 15, while KuCoin says Fri Oct 16, so confirm on the Fed calendar.

Fri Oct 16: Possible Warsh date per KuCoin. The Fed's pre-FOMC blackout is expected to start Oct 17, ahead of the Oct 27-28 meeting (hike odds were below 20% as of Oct 9). Other reporters named in week-ahead previews include Delta (iTiger 'What to Watch This Week'). Netflix's date was not confirmed (null).

picks.angle: This is the strongest momentum name on the board and the only AI-infrastructure pick in the lineup. It ranked number one on the quant composite (relative strength 98, all 8 trend checks passed), and it was the one name all three ballots picked. News backs the move: a record AI-server backlog of about $95 billion, full-year guidance raised to about $192 billion, Mizuho's $650 target on Oct 6, and the wider AI-capex cycle. Frame it as a stock to hold above $565 while waiting for a breakout over $595.51, not one to chase. Make the caveats clear on air: volume is light, Silver Lake keeps selling around the current price, and the Street's targets are mixed. Fresh check: Tuesday's Oct 13 close was not available. If DELL closes below $565, reframe it as a pullback watch rather than a momentum leader.
picks.business_one_liner: Dell sells PCs, storage and data-center servers. AI servers built on Nvidia chips are now its main growth engine.

levels.how_to_say: The pivot is the 52-week high of about $596. We want a close above it on at least about one and a half times normal volume before calling it the next leg. Mizuho's $650 is the upside marker. Near-term support is $565, Monday's low, and it traded about there after hours. Hold $565 and wait for $596. Don't chase it. Invalidation is a close below about $523, roughly nine percent under Monday's close. That's a wide stop for a mega-cap, so size down. Deeper support is the 50-day average, near $506.

upcoming: Tue Oct 13: check the close against $565 support. The last print was Monday after-hours at about $566. A close below $565 means reframing DELL as a pullback watch.

picks.risk: This is a crowded, high-beta AI-hardware trade with soft confirmation. Volume is running at about 0.63x average. Silver Lake keeps selling right at the current price ($575-584). Consensus targets cluster near or just above the price. Monday's memory/semi selloff and the after-hours drift to about $566 put the $565 support at risk of breaking early in the week. A soft AI-capex comment from ASML (Oct 14) or TSMC (Oct 15) would hit DELL in sympathy. Invalidation sits about 9.3% below the close (about 7.6% below the after-hours price), so size the position down.

picks.angle: A lesser-known leader. A digital-manufacturing marketplace riding the reshoring and industrial-tech theme. Relative strength is 95, the RS line is at a new high, and it just broke out to a record. The move is backed by fundamentals: Q2 revenue up 41%, and three firms set $120 targets in September. picks.angle: This is the non-AI leader that best fits Rule 7, because it has both news and the whole industry behind it. Refining margins are near records, the refiner group is moving together, and there has been a wave of analyst target raises, ending with Barclays at $488 on Monday. It also moves the lineup's factor exposure away from growth and AI. Present it as the leader of a group that is already moving, not as a fresh breakout. The preferred entry is a hold of $455, not chasing a move through the $470 record.
picks.business_one_liner: Marathon Petroleum is the largest independent oil refiner in the US. It makes gasoline, diesel and jet fuel, and it owns a pipeline arm through MPLX. It makes its money on the gap between what crude costs and what refined fuel sells for, which is called the crack spread.
facts: Marathon Petroleum closed Monday at about $459, up almost 1% on the day.
Early Monday it traded up to about $467, then gave some back. It closed below its record intraday high of $470, which was set last week.
Its record close is about $463, set last Thursday.
The stock is up about 6% in the past week.
It has gone from about $300 in early August to about $459 now, a gain of more than 50% in roughly two months.
It sits about 21% above its 50-day moving average. That is extended, but still inside our 25% limit.
On Monday, Barclays raised its price target to $488 from $321 and kept an Overweight rating.
That came on top of a wave of target raises in early October, including TD Cowen and BMO.
Not everyone is chasing it. Mizuho is at Neutral with a $457 target, which is about where the stock trades now.
Jefferies raised its target only to $433, which is below the current price.
The average Wall Street target is about $400, well below the stock. The stock has run ahead of most analysts.
The key refining margin, the 3-2-1 crack spread, was about $65 a barrel on October 6. That is near the widest since records began in 1986.
That margin has eased a bit from its late-September peak, so it is near the record but no longer climbing.
US diesel margins set records above $100 a barrel in September.
Diesel supply is tight. New York diesel inventories are at a four-year low.
Diesel flows out of the Persian Gulf are reported to be down about 80% from a year ago.
This is a group move, not just one stock. Valero and Phillips 66 have rallied too, and four refiners logged six straight weekly gains in September.
Analysts expect windfall third-quarter profits for the refiners.
Marathon reports third-quarter results on Tuesday, November 3, which is after our window.
Headlines can hit this group fast. Last Thursday, President Trump said Russia would supply diesel to world markets. Diesel futures fell 4% and Marathon fell about 2%.
This pick is energy, not AI. It gives the lineup a different kind of exposure.

levels.how_to_say: The level to watch is $470, the record intraday high. A close above it would confirm the breakout. Support is about $455, last Friday's close.
